book_title: Petrichor: The Scent of a New Beginning
subject_line: Jola Balogun and the Oshogbo mission school in Petrichor
email_body:
Dear Ayo,
Petrichor opening in 1976 at a mission school in Oshogbo, with Jola Balogun carrying his trauma forward from there, is a striking starting point for a novel that went on to the 2025 Nigeria Prize for Literature longlist. I would be curious to hear why you anchored Jola's story in that year and that school, and how your daily work as an editor in Ibadan shapes the way you revise your own fiction.

subject_line: Casting Sango as a woman in Sanya
email_body:
Dear Oyin,
The choice at the heart of Sanya, retelling the story of Sango through a female protagonist, is the detail the Nigeria Prize judges singled out as daring when the book won in 2025, and it is a remarkable move for a debut. I would love to ask how you decided which parts of the Sango tradition to keep intact and which to bend, and whether the Yoruba stories you encountered growing up in Ibadan shaped that balance.

subject_line: A ghost narrator and four track stars in Fine Dreams
email_body:
Dear Linda,
Fine Dreams hands its story of four teenage track stars, kidnapped while studying for their exams, to a ghost narrator, and that choice gives the novel an unusual vantage on a fictional town and school. The book won the Juniper Prize for Fiction and was longlisted for the 2025 Nigeria Prize for Literature. I would like to ask when the ghost arrived as narrator during the writing, and what that voice let you say that a living witness could not.

subject_line: The finalist year of Terminal Maladies
email_body:
Dear Okwudili,
Terminal Maladies, your debut collection, reached the finalist lists of both the Lambda Literary Award for Gay Poetry and the Hurston/Wright Legacy Award, two prizes that read a book from quite different angles. I would be interested to hear how you think about the title's language of illness across the collection, and whether being recognised by those two communities changed how you understand what the poems are doing.

subject_line: Affection and Other Accidents and The Lagos Review
email_body:
Dear Dami,
Affection and Other Accidents, your third poetry collection, came out with Radi8 Books in 2022, a few years after you and Toni Kan founded The Lagos Review in 2019. I would be glad to ask how editing a magazine that reads so many other writers has changed the way you assemble your own collections, and what the word accidents is doing in that title for you.
